families.name: Masthead
families.summary: The head of a page or app. The header is a glass panel with a large caption: number left in the tone, title right, an etched rule under both. --bar is the one-line top bar, the client's round logo first (__mark); --split puts the caption and the tools in two pills with the page between them. The lockup is a hero's sign-off: the wordmark, an etched line from it to the edge, and the headline split by the line, its rolling word in the root colour's family. --app is the app bar on the sidebar's frost panel: a lead with the sidebar cube, summary chips with cards, and tools. Three layouts of it share that panel and content: centred (as is), --app-inline (a one-line readout after the lead, etched rules between items) and --app-tiles (each item a sidebar row tile with its cube, the tools past an etched rule). --app-crumbs puts a crumb trail where the lead was, with no summary: an area crumb that opens the areas and one record crumb (its cube and name) that opens a switcher; two levels at most, a soft progress arrow between them, the drop-down chevron on hover only. Shown over a picture so the frost reads.

Why it matters

Most systems fail at the seams, not the center

Each tool works on its own. The cost shows up where data crosses from one to the next: re-keyed orders, stale reports, follow-ups nobody owns.

The approach

  • Map every hand-off between systems
  • Fix the model before adding automation
  • Instrument it so problems surface first

families.name: Form section
families.summary: fh-panel-section--form. A section where a person edits the record in place: one form with one fieldset of Firehorse fields (fh-money included, and fh-panel-section__slot for a field the host supplies), then the actions row. A section whose slot holds a field that renders its own form uses <div class="fh-panel-section__form" role="group" aria-labelledby="…"> as its body instead of the form: never put a form inside a form. A field's read only value, such as "ends in 4f2a", goes in its hint. States are markup only: data-dirty on the section is changed, aria-busy on the form with the save button disabled is saving, one fh-status in the actions row is saved (or an error that belongs to no field), fh-field__error is a field error, and a disabled fieldset with a one line note above it is locked. sidecar.js sets data-dirty on the section and the sidecar; a dirty sidecar fires a cancelable fh:sidecar-before-close before it closes or swaps record. The actions stack under 36rem.

families.summary: fh-panel-section--stage. Report policy

660 words17 Nov 2026

How a relay report is written

A relay report is the record of one run. It names the relay, the worktree and the branch, then what was built and what each check printed. It is written once, when the run ends, and it does not carry a key. The person who reads it should be able to see the work without opening the branch.

The timetable is one line per step. Each line starts with the local time the step finished. The time comes from the clock, never from a guess. A step that is still running is not a finished line, and a time you did not read is not a time you may print.

House voice is plain. Say what the section holds and what a person can do with it. Leave out a claim you did not check. If a screen was not opened, say that the screen was not opened. A guess dressed up as a result is worse than a gap.

What goes in

Start with the run context as it was handed over. Then the timetable. Then the codes you issued, and the result of each check. End with the words the spec asks for. Do not add a second ending, and do not rewrite the context block.

Commands go in with a short view of their output. Trim a long log to the lines that show the result. If a command was not allowed, say so and do not invent a result. A skipped check is a result of its own: name it, and say why it was skipped.

A fix after a commit is a second commit. Nothing is amended, stashed, reset or pushed. The hook runs. A message names the kind and the spec, so a later reader can find the run from the history alone.

What stays out
  • No key, token or password, even when a check printed one.
  • No path outside the worktree, and no read of a file that holds a secret.
  • No claim that a test passed unless the output says it passed.
  • No second layout, and no colour, radius or shadow of your own.
  • No retired code brought back, and no code renumbered to make a row fit.
  • No part from outside Firehorse. If a part is missing, stop and say so.
How the checks read

Read the result from the command, not from memory. A line that says skip is expected when the diff does not touch what that check reads. Do not run a skipped check by hand to fill the report. The sweep runs the wide checks once per wave.

The screen tier checks the page. At a narrow width the page itself does not scroll sideways: a long line of code, and a deep tree, scroll inside the section. The report says so only after a check, or it says the check was not run.

The same rules apply to a policy, a long reply and a spec. Past about 24 lines the text folds, and Show all opens it in place. A short note does not fold. Headings step down so they sit under the section title, in the prose roles.

Records this policy names
RecordKindWhere
Relay reportnotethe run folder
Timetablesectioninside the report
Index ledgerrecordthe package root
A line the report may quote

Chips show only while the section is closed. For a document they are the word count and the date it was updated. The count is the words in the body, including the headings, the table and the code.

When the run cannot finish, the report still gets written. It says what is left, and it ends by saying the report is incomplete. Updated with the sections for code, a document and a tree.
